title: Proactive capacity modeling and stable autoscaling for embeddings
creator: Priya Patel
summary: Design and implement a proactive capacity model and a stabilizing autoscaler for the embeddings endpoint. The goal is to reduce tail latency and outages during bursts, maintain predictable cost-per-embedding, and provide strong SLO adherence across tenant classes.
problem_statement: Current embedding endpoints suffer from high tail latency and oscillatory autoscaling when bursty traffic interacts with token-variable requests. This causes customer-visible throttles, increased p99 latency, and inefficient GPU utilization. Existing queue smoothing and burst headroom heuristics mitigate symptoms but don't address demand forecasting, warm-pool sizing, or priority preemption needs for tiered customers.
goals: Reduce p99 latency for embeddings by >=25% under representative burst profiles
Eliminate autoscaler oscillations that cause >2x spin-up/spin-down churn per hour
Provide deterministic capacity guarantees for P0/P1 tenants via warm pools
Limit embedding tail cost increase to <=10% while improving throughput efficiency
Expose observability and control surface for capacity forecasts and forced failovers
acceptance_criteria: Benchmark suite (see dashboards) shows p50/p95/p99 improvement relative to baseline for the standard dev prompt set
Autoscaler passes 48-hour soak without >3 scaling oscillation events per tenant group
Warm-pool size heuristics provide <5% cold-start rate for VIP tenants during simulated bursts
Rate-limiter and token-throttling logic enforced and covered by integration tests
Rollout playbook validated in canary region with rollback under 10 minutes
design_notes: Move from reactive CPU/GPU utilization threshold autoscaling to a hybrid model that combines short-term demand forecasting (5-15 min horizon) with safe headroom sizing
Introduce tenant-class priority queues with weighted token budgets — allows VIP tenants to preempt capacity during sustained contention
Implement dynamic token throttling per request that factors token count, tenant class, and current estimated active KV cache hit rate
Keep queueing local to an availability zone to limit cross-AZ tail latency; route overflow to compatible lower-cost model variants instead of remote scaling where appropriate
Trade-off: forecasting reduces cold starts but requires stable load signals; in cases of high unpredictability we fallback to conservative headroom to preserve SLOs
progress_updates: 2026-02-18: RFC drafted and shared with infra and product for feedback (confluence: https://confluence.redwood.company/display/ENG/ENG-31780+-+Capacity+Model).
2026-02-25: Spike completed: 10-hour synthetic burst test using ARIMA-based short-term predictor reduced cold starts by 42% compared to threshold autoscaler.
2026-03-03: Implemented priority queue prototype in staging; observed fair-share degradation when a single tenant produced 90% of requests — added weighted token budgets to address.
2026-03-10: Canary rollout plan approved by SRE and PM; preparing Grafana dashboards and synthetic load scripts for regional canary.
open_questions: What minimum headroom percentage do we guarantee for low-tier tenants during VIP burst preemption?
Should forecast model be run centrally (control plane) or locally per AZ? Latency vs model staleness trade-offs.
How to map tenant SLAs to warm-pool sizing algorithm for multi-tenant GPUs with varied affinity?
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Unit and integration tests in CI, validate throttling invariants
Stage 1: Deploy forecasting + warm pool sizing to staging region; run 72-hour soak with recorded production traces
Stage 2: Canary region rollout (10% traffic) with throttles mostly passive; monitor p99 and scaling churn
Stage 3: Enable active preemption for VIP tenants in canary; observe cost and latency impact
Stage 4: Full rollout with ramp and automated rollback triggers defined in SRE playbook
monitoring_playbook: Alert: embedding-p99 > baseline_threshold for 10m -> trigger autoscaler-inspector run and scale-up evaluation
Alert: >3 scaling oscillations in 1h -> pause autoscaling and switch to conservative headroom mode
Runbook: capture heap snapshot and request traces for offending tenant; compare to forecasted demand
Rollback: disable forecast-based autoscaling and return to utilization-threshold autoscaler
estimated_cost_impact: Expected +7% GPU infra cost at peak due to warm pools for VIPs; estimated net per-embedding cost reduction of ~12% after improved batching and reduced KV cache misses
risks: Forecast model underfits new spike patterns leading to underprovision and SLO violations
Priority preemption could over-throttle low-tier customers and cause retention impact
Increased complexity in autoscaler may lengthen incident resolution time
Warm pools increase idle GPU hours and contractual cost exposure for Dedicated customers
mitigations: A/B test forecast-based autoscaler vs baseline for low-risk tenant set before broad rollout
Expose tenant-level throttling visibility in Console so customers can self-adjust request patterns
Keep a simplified fallback path (utilization threshold autoscaler) that can be enabled with a single feature flag
Negotiate Dedicated warm-pool contracts with flexible billing or convertible reserved capacity
notes_for_code_review: Ensure autoscaler state machine is idempotent across control plane restarts
Validate metrics emitted for every decision: forecast, headroom, warm-pool adjust, preemption events
Include unit tests for weighted token budgeting and integration test covering tenant preemption scenarios
closure_criteria: All acceptance criteria met and sign-off from SRE, Product, and Cost team
Canary region stable for 7 days with no >1 critical incident related to embeddings scaling
Documentation and Console controls shipped (forecast toggle, warm-pool sizing UI)
